newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer, further gains seen tough.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer, further gains seen tough.

text.p: London cocoa futures clawed back losses and ended firmer on Wednesday, but traders said the market remained vulnerable to overhead resistance.
"It's just running with orders. There's nothing to get worked up about," said one trader.

The benchmark March position spent most of the session at contract lows of 930-932 stg, also a seven-month low on continuation basis -- but racked up gains in the afternoon to close at 940 stg, seven higher from Tuesday.
It was also helped by sterling which eased from a peak of $1.6495 on Wednesday to around $1.6380/90.
The technically-friendly close has pulled the market toward the upper end of a downtrend channel in place since the middle of October.

March is now facing a strong resistance point along that channel at 951 which, according to chart analysts, may prove difficult to clear. Players brushed aside higher cocoa purchase figures in the first week of the Ghanaian season. These stood at 32,130 tonnes by October 17, up from 22,843 tonnes in the same period of 1995/96.
They said a delayed start to the season distorted the arrivals flow which could be expected to take shape from the end of November.
Physical demand remained slow on Wednesday with buyers sidelined partly due to sterling's strength against the dollar and other European currencies in which cocoa is usually priced on the Continent.
Turnover was a modest 4,553 lots. On the switches Dec/March traded wider at 34 stg whereas March/May was valued at 19, traders said.
